translationRepairs: In the second year, seeing the times turning dangerous, he memorialized asking the throne to issue an edict inviting open counsel. He wrote in part: 'Secret-society rebels in western Guangdong have been in turmoil for two years. Generals have been sent against them, yet there has been little success; the rebels have even besieged the provincial capital and grown wildly bold.

In the second year, seeing the times turning dangerous, he memorialized asking the throne to issue an edict inviting open counsel. He wrote in part: 'Secret-society rebels in Guangxi have been in turmoil for two years. Generals have been sent against them, yet there has been little success; the rebels have even besieged the provincial capital and grown wildly bold.
粵西 in this Xianfeng memorial names Guangxi (the western Yue), not Guangdong; the proposed 'western Guangxi' still reads as a subregion of Guangxi rather than the province.

In the second year, because current affairs were perilous, he memorialized requesting an edict calling for candid advice, saying in summary: 'The secret-society bandits in western Guangdong have risen in revolt; for two years generals have been dispatched on campaign without notable success, and the rebels have even besieged the provincial capital and run rampant.

In the second year, because current affairs were perilous, he memorialized requesting an edict calling for candid advice, saying in summary: 'The secret-society bandits in Guangxi have risen in revolt; for two years generals have been dispatched on campaign without notable success, and the rebels have even besieged the provincial capital and run rampant.
The literal field repeats 粵西 as Guangdong; replace with Guangxi, not the still-misleading calque 'western Guangxi'.

When Emperor Wenzong took the throne, an edict called for men of talent. Vice Minister Hou Tong and Governor-General Lu Jianying jointly recommended Minghe, and he was promoted to metropolitan prefect of Shuntian.

When Emperor Wenzong took the throne, an edict called for men of talent. Vice Minister of Revenue Hou Tong and Governor-General Lu Jianying jointly recommended Minghe, and he was promoted to metropolitan prefect of Shuntian.
戶部侍郎 identifies Hou Tong's Revenue portfolio, which the idiomatic English omitted while the Chinese and the literal rendering both keep it.
In the triennial examination he placed second class, was promoted to reader, and then transferred to assistant director of the Academy.
In the triennial examination he placed second class, was promoted to admonisher of the heir apparent (zanshan), and then transferred to companion of the heir apparent (zhongyun).
贊善 and 中允 are heir-apparent household ranks, not a Hanlin reader or academy assistant director; the proposed mix of a glossed 'adviser (zanshan)' with bare 'zhongyun' is incomplete and awkward.
In the triennial examination he ranked second class, was promoted to reader, and transferred to assistant director of the Academy.
In the triennial examination he ranked second class, was promoted to zanshan (admonisher of the heir apparent), and transferred to zhongyun (companion of the heir apparent).
The same 贊善/中允 mistranslation appears in the literal field; bare pinyin without English office sense is not complete natural English.
In the twenty-fifth year, when mourning ended, he was again appointed educational commissioner of Guangdong before taking another post, and rose step by step to grand secretary.
In the twenty-fifth year, when mourning ended, he was again appointed educational commissioner of Guangdong before taking another post, and rose step by step to academician of the Grand Secretariat.
內閣學士 is an academician of the Grand Secretariat; 大學士 is the distinct grand-secretary rank, so the original inflates the office.
In the twenty-fifth year, when mourning ended, before receiving a new appointment he again supervised education in Guangdong and was promoted step by step to grand secretary of the Grand Secretariat.
In the twenty-fifth year, when mourning ended, before receiving a new appointment he again supervised education in Guangdong and was promoted step by step to academician of the Grand Secretariat.
The literal English likewise renders 內閣學士 as grand secretary; academician of the Grand Secretariat is the correct office.
Emperor Xuanzong was delighted, treated it as a singular achievement, and ennobled Governor-General Xu Guangjin as marquis and Governor Ye Mingchen as baron.
Emperor Xuanzong was delighted, treated it as a singular achievement, and ennobled Governor-General Xu Guangjin as viscount and Governor Ye Mingchen as baron.
錫封…子爵 names a viscount; marquis would be 侯爵, so the original noble rank is wrong.
Emperor Xuanzong was delighted, regarded it as a singular achievement, and ennobled Governor-General Xu Guangjin as marquis and Governor Ye Mingchen as baron.
Emperor Xuanzong was delighted, regarded it as a singular achievement, and ennobled Governor-General Xu Guangjin as viscount and Governor Ye Mingchen as baron.
The literal field repeats 子爵 as marquis; viscount matches the Chinese rank.
The rebels tunneled under the old site of Songzhen Humen and blasted the wall. The city fell, and Xi drowned himself.
The rebels tunneled under the old site of the Song Zhenhu Gate and blasted the wall. The city fell, and Xi drowned himself.
宋鎮湖門故址 is the former site of the Song Zhenhu Gate, not a fused place-name Songzhen Humen.

In the triennial examination he placed first class, was promoted to junior tutor of the heir apparent, was promoted ahead of schedule to grand secretary, and served as educational commissioner of Jiangsu.

In the triennial examination he placed first class, was promoted to junior tutor of the heir apparent, was promoted ahead of schedule to academician of the Grand Secretariat, and served as educational commissioner of Jiangsu.
超遷內閣學士 is promotion to academician of the Grand Secretariat, not to grand secretary (大學士).
The rebels watched for an opening in Huizhou and Ningguo, while the governor, posted at Luzhou, could not cover both regions.
The rebels were urgently probing Huizhou and Ningguo, while the governor, posted at Luzhou, could not cover both regions.
窺…急 marks urgent designs on Huizhou and Ningguo; the original drops 急, but 'pressed' overtranslates 窺, which is watching or probing rather than already assaulting.
When his mother died, he was granted leave from mourning to remain with the army and was told that after mourning he would await appointment as third-rank metropolitan official.
When his mother died, mourning was set aside so that he could remain with the army, and he was told that after the mourning term he would await appointment as a third-rank metropolitan official.
奪情留軍 means mourning was set aside so he remained with the army, the reverse of being granted mourning leave.
When his mother died, he was granted leave from mourning to remain with the army and was ordered that after mourning ended he would await appointment as third-rank metropolitan official.

When his mother died, mourning was set aside so that he could remain with the army, and he was ordered that after the mourning term ended he would await appointment as a third-rank metropolitan official.
The literal 'granted leave from mourning' inverts 奪情; setting mourning aside to keep him on duty is the sense of the Chinese.

In the second year of Tongzhi the rebel Hui Ma Rong feigned surrender, entered the city and killed Governor Pan Duo, then slaughtered and plundered freely. Cong was killed and was posthumously granted the rank of censor-in-chief of the right.

In the second year of Tongzhi the rebel Hui Ma Rong feigned surrender, entered the city and killed Governor-General Pan Duo, then slaughtered and plundered freely. Cong was killed and was posthumously granted the rank of censor-in-chief of the right.
戕總督潘鐸 names Pan Duo as governor-general (總督), not provincial governor (巡撫).

In the second year of Tongzhi the rebel Hui Ma Rong feigned surrender, entered the city and killed Governor Pan Duo, slaughtered and plundered freely, and Cong was killed; he was posthumously granted the rank of censor-in-chief of the right.

In the second year of Tongzhi the rebel Hui Ma Rong feigned surrender, entered the city and killed Governor-General Pan Duo, slaughtered and plundered freely, and Cong was killed; he was posthumously granted the rank of censor-in-chief of the right.
The literal English makes the same 總督/governor error; Governor-General matches the Chinese office.

When word reached the court, Emperor Wenzong, noting that with the fall of Wuchang the city's entire civil and military corps had died in service, granted especially generous mourning honors, posthumously made him vice minister, ordered a special shrine built, granted the hereditary rank of Commandant of Cavalry, and gave him the posthumous title Wenjie, 'Cultured Integrity.'

When word reached the court, Emperor Wenzong, noting that with the fall of Wuchang the city's entire civil and military corps had died in service, granted especially generous mourning honors, posthumously made him vice minister, ordered a special shrine built, granted the hereditary rank of Commandant of Cavalry, and gave him the posthumous title Wenjie, 'Cultured Steadfastness.'
The posthumous title is 文介, not 文節; 'Cultured Integrity' glosses 節 rather than 介.
In the third year he was promoted in succession to grand secretary and vice minister of War, and served as educational commissioner of Anhui.
In the third year he was promoted in succession to academician of the Grand Secretariat and vice minister of War, and served as educational commissioner of Anhui.
連擢內閣學士 is academician of the Grand Secretariat, not grand secretary (大學士).
In the third year he was promoted in succession to grand secretary of the Grand Secretariat and vice minister of War, and supervised education in Anhui.
In the third year he was promoted in succession to academician of the Grand Secretariat and vice minister of War, and supervised education in Anhui.
The literal field likewise inflates 內閣學士 into grand secretary of the Grand Secretariat.
He became a metropolitan graduate in the twenty-fifth year of Daoguang, entered the Hanlin Academy as a bachelor, was appointed a compiler, and was transferred to assistant director of the Academy.
He became a metropolitan graduate in the twenty-fifth year of Daoguang, entered the Hanlin Academy as a bachelor, was appointed a compiler, and was transferred to Advisor of the Heir Apparent.
遷中允 is transfer to the heir-apparent household rank zhongyun, not assistant director of the Hanlin Academy.

In the twenty-fifth year of Daoguang he passed the metropolitan examination, was selected as a bachelor of the Hanlin Academy, was appointed compiler, and was transferred to assistant director of the Academy.

In the twenty-fifth year of Daoguang he passed the metropolitan examination, was selected as a bachelor of the Hanlin Academy, was appointed compiler, and was transferred to Advisor of the Heir Apparent.
The literal English repeats the 中允/academy-assistant-director error; Advisor of the Heir Apparent restores the office.

An edict praised his unyielding integrity and the terrible cruelty of his death, posthumously made him grand secretary, enshrined him in the Hall of Loyalty and Devotion in the capital and in Anhui and Jiangsu, granted the hereditary rank of Commandant of Cavalry, and gave him the posthumous title Wenjie, 'Cultured Integrity.'

An edict praised his unyielding integrity and the terrible cruelty of his death, posthumously made him academician of the Grand Secretariat, enshrined him in the Hall of Loyalty and Devotion in the capital and in Anhui and Jiangsu, granted the hereditary rank of Commandant of Cavalry, and gave him the posthumous title Wenjie, 'Cultured Integrity.'
贈內閣學士 is a posthumous Grand Secretariat academician, not 大學士; 'bachelor of the Grand Secretariat' confuses 學士 with 庶吉士.
He was posthumously made grand secretary, given the posthumous title Wenjie, 'Cultured Integrity,' and a special shrine was built for him in Guilin.
He was posthumously made academician of the Grand Secretariat, given the posthumous title Wenjie, 'Cultured Integrity,' and a special shrine was built for him in Guilin.
贈內閣學士 is again an academician, not a grand secretary; bachelor is the wrong English equivalent of 學士 here.
